takeaways.text: Net sales hit $1,976.4M, up 21.2% YoY from $1,630.2M — the 14th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and the second straight above 20%. Ninja grew 27.7% to $1,083.2M and Shark 14.2% to $893.2M. By category, Cooking and Beverage Appliances rose 36.6% on the Ninja Luxe Café espresso machine and the Ninja Crispi, Beauty and Home Environment rose 45.8%, Food Preparation 18.3% and Cleaning Appliances 4.1%. International sales grew 25.2% and Domestic 19.4%.
takeaways.title: Fourteenth straight quarter of double-digit growth

takeaways.text: Gross margin jumped to 59.2% from 50.1% a year ago, helped by $243.8M of IEEPA tariff-refund claims, less $45.2M payable to factory partners. Even stripping those out, Adjusted Gross Margin rose 560 basis points to 55.9%. Operating income rose 68.5% to $442.9M, a 22.4% margin, and Adjusted Operating Income was $425.5M. Net income rose 79.3% to $338.4M, or $2.39 per diluted share; Adjusted Net Income rose 55.1% to $330.9M.
takeaways.title: Margins jumped — mostly on a tariff refund

takeaways.text: SharkNinja raised its full-year outlook: net sales now expected up 18.0% to 19.0% (was 16.0% to 17.0%), Adjusted Net Income per diluted share of $6.65 to $6.75, and Adjusted EBITDA of $1,380M to $1,391M. In Q3 it recognized $109.6M of 2025-duty refunds out of a ~$247.1M total claim accepted by U.S. Customs and Border Protection, with about $35.8M more expected in Q4 2026.
takeaways.title: Outlook raised into the holidays

verdict: SharkNinja grew sales 21% to $1.98 billion and net income jumped 79% to $338 million, with a $110 million tariff refund flattering the quarter — even stripping it out, adjusted profit still rose 55%.
